subject.title: feat(browser): send pages to OpenClaw from the Chrome extension

question: Should OpenClaw adopt first-party Chrome page sharing, including its new browser-ingress path and additive `system-event-runtime` SDK export, once the default lazy-service lifecycle is repaired?
rationale: The mechanical lifecycle fix is clear, but accepting a persistent browser-to-agent ingress feature and public SDK surface is a maintainer product and API-contract decision.

options.title: Sponsor the feature after lifecycle repair
options.body: Move sink ownership into the default Gateway lazy-service path, add regression coverage and normal-path live proof, then review the browser-ingress and SDK contract.

options.title: Defer the product surface
options.body: Keep the branch open only if maintainers want a first-party page-sharing feature rather than an external extension or plugin path.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the feature after lifecycle repair
recommendation.body: Move sink ownership into the default Gateway lazy-service path, add regression coverage and normal-path live proof, then review the browser-ingress and SDK contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The current implementation and follow-up commits place this contributor closest to the browser feature’s intended behavior and repair boundary.
